reader.requirement: At --std 85 an indexed file's file control entry admits RESERVE integer-1 [AREA | AREAS] (once, in any order after SELECT) with the Sequential I-O rule (§1985:VII.2.9.3 GR1): the number of input-output areas allocated equals integer-1, an integer literal neither signed nor zero (§1985:III.2), and without the clause the count is the implementor's; the file must still process its records under every access mode.

edition-consulted.switches: ConstructRegistry.IsAvailable(constant-entry-2002): at 85 a word in the integer-1 position is refused as 'not an integer literal' (no constant-names), at 2023 a constant-name is admitted
dialectLevel < 2002 picks the §1985:III.2 wording of the zero refusal; the refusal itself is the same

reader.edition-search: grep 'Edition|DialectLevel|ConstructRegistry' in FileControlBinder.cs RESERVE arm, SequentialIoEmitter.EmitReserveRegistration, KeyedConnector.Attach (none); the area count path is edition-free
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the area count; the integer-1 operand admits a constant-name from 2002 only (refused at 85, as 85 has no constant entry)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb643 runs RESERVE 1 AREA on a random-access indexed file; RESERVE on dynamic and sequential access indexed files, the AREA-word omitted, the clause before ORGANIZATION, and the refusal forms (signed, zero, decimal, NO ALTERNATE, duplicate) at --std 85 are not exercised

probes.printed: RAND 150 00 / COUNT 300 10 / D EE / Y 7   00 / Z 9   00
probes.expected: RESERVE 3 AREAS (dynamic, clause written before ORGANIZATION), RESERVE 1 AREA (sequential), RESERVE 2 with no AREA word (random) each compile; 300 records of 43 bytes (beyond 3 areas) written, randomly read and rewritten, read back sequentially: 300 then 10; records unchanged

probes.printed: RESERVE 0: COBOL2386 (§1985:III.2 nonzero); -1 and +2: COBOL0312/COBOL1970; 2.0: COBOL5506; NO ALTERNATE AREA: COBOL5506; AREAS alone: COBOL5506; RESERVE 2 RESERVE 3: COBOL2423; 524288: COBOL2897 (implementor limit)
probes.expected: integer-1 is an integer literal neither signed nor zero, the clause appears once; a limit refusal is the implementor's (§2023 limit, the 85 count is exact)

probes.printed: --std 85: RESERVE W (data item): COBOL1547 'not an integer literal ... COBOL-85 has no constant-name'; 01 K CONSTANT: COBOL0900 requires COBOL-2002; --std 2023: COBOL1547 'not a defined constant-name'
probes.expected: integer-1 is a literal at 85; constant-names are a later edition's operand class

citations.check: OK  §1985:IX.2.3.4 GR6  (2.3.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR6
OK  §1985:VII.2.9.3 GR1  (2.9.3 General Rules)  the text is in GR1

reader.notes: One fileReserveClause serves every organization; FileControlBinder stores the count, EmitAreaRegistrations (called by every registering arm, indexed included) emits RegisterReserve, and KeyedConnector.Attach sizes the store handle's page cache from InputOutputAreas. The count is not observable to a program beyond records passing unchanged, which the probes show.

refuter.evidence: r6a.cob at --std 85: SELECT OPTIONAL A1 RESERVE 007 AREAS ASSIGN ... (RESERVE before ASSIGN, leading zeros; §1985:IX.2.3.3 SR1 any order after SELECT) dynamic access: OPEN I-O of the absent optional file 05, 500 records of 64 bytes written in descending key order, START > '0000' and READ NEXT returns all 500 in ascending order then 10; SELECT A2 ... FILE STATUS, INDEXED, RECORD KEY, ALTERNATE RECORD KEY WITH DUPLICATES, then RESERVE 200 AREA (singular word, after the key clauses), ACCESS MODE RANDOM: WRITE then random READ 00 X. The compiler also enforces the 1985 operand rules on the way (numeric RECORD KEY refused COBOL0863 §1985:IX.2.7.3 SR2; unterminated WRITE in an inline PERFORM refused). Read FileControlBinder.cs#BindFileControl RESERVE arm: no edition switch; the COBOL2897 limit (524287 areas, one 4096-byte area each, not probed at host scale) is permitted at 85 by §1985:I.1.7 (limits 'may prevent the successful translation of some programs'), though its message cites §2023:4.2.15 at --std 85 (wording only, not this rule). cite.py: OK §1985:IX.2.3.4 GR6; OK §1985:VII.2.9.3 GR1; OK §1985:IX.2.3.3 SR1; OK §1985:I.1.7.
